tests.name: Numerical Reasoning Test 10
tests.subtitle: AssessmentDay source test
tests.description: A 30-question mixed-difficulty numerical reasoning test using sales, shares, mobile packages, consultancy finances, company revenue, and population data.
tests.instructions:
This numerical reasoning test comprises 30 questions, and you will have 30 minutes in which to correctly answer as many as you can. Calculators are permitted for this test, and it is recommended you have some rough paper to work on.

You will have to work quickly and accurately to perform well in this test. If you don't know the answer to a question, leave it and come back to it if you have time. Each question will have five possible answers, one of which is correct. You may click Back and Next during the test to review or skip questions.

You can submit your test at any time. If the time limit is up before you click submit the test will automatically be submitted with the answers you have selected. It is recommended to keep working until the time limit is up.

Try to find a time and place where you will not be interrupted during the test. The test will begin on the next page.

questions.prompt: If worldwide sales comprise US sales, EU sales and Far Eastern sales, which products had the highest annual Far Eastern Sales?
questions.explanation: Far Eastern sales are worldwide minus annual US and EU sales. Product A: 320 - (54.5 + 50.5) - (90.5 + 91.4) = £33.1 million, higher than B £29.7m, C £31.3m, D £25.9m and E £15.1m.

questions.prompt: For the five products combined there was a difference between total annual Sales and the total annual Sales Target. How did this difference compare for the US and the EU?
questions.explanation: US target total = 110 + 120 + 120 + 150 + 150 = £650m; US sales total = £645.3m, so the difference is £4.7m. EU target total = £910m; EU sales total = £899.6m, so the difference is £10.4m.

questions.prompt: If the annual EU sales for Products B and C both comprise online: offline sales in a ratio of 2:3 then what are the online EU sales for Products B and C combined?
How much US and EU annual sales tax is due for Products B, C and D combined (to the nearest £million)?
questions.explanation: Combined US sales exceed £130m, so US tax is £130m × 24% = £31.2m. Combined EU sales are 150 + 180.2 + 203.5 = £533.7m, taxed at 22% = £117.414m. Total = £148.614m, which rounds to £149m.

questions.prompt: Which of the following represents the smallest amount?
options: Product B’s change in EU sales between Jan-June and July-Dec
Product E’s change in US sales between Jan-June and July-Dec
Average US Product A sales per month (July-Dec)
Average US Product C sales per month (Jan-June)

questions.prompt: A rights issue brings an additional 10% of Studt Systems shares to the market. If the current price per share drops by 8%, what is Studt Systems’ new company value (to the nearest £million)?
questions.explanation: New shares = 55m × 1.10 = 60.5m. New price = £3 × 0.92 = £2.76. Company value = 60.5m × £2.76 = £166.98m, which rounds to £167m.

questions.prompt: At current prices, if the owner of 150,000 Studt Systems shares collected the dividend then sold the shares, how many Tombe shares could they buy with the proceeds (to the nearest 10,000)?
questions.explanation: Studt proceeds per share = £3.00 + £0.08 dividend = £3.08. Total proceeds = 150,000 × £3.08 = £462,000. At £1.85 per Tombe share this buys 249,729.7 shares, or 250,000 to the nearest 10,000.

questions.prompt: Which share has changed in price by the largest amount since the previous day?
questions.explanation: Previous price equals previous company value divided by shares. Absolute changes are Relf £0.25; Studt about £0.109; Xan about £0.053; IWE |£200m/114m - £1.48| ≈ £0.274. IWE has the largest change.

questions.prompt: A day trader bought 50,000 Tombe shares at last month’s low, received the Tombe dividend and then sold all these shares at last month’s high. What was the approximate percentage gain or loss?
questions.explanation: Tombe was bought at £1.70 and produced £2.03 sale proceeds plus £0.10 dividend, a gain of £0.43 per share. £0.43/£1.70 × 100 = 25.3% profit.

questions.prompt: A trader has £185,000 to invest and decides to invest this money equally across the 5 shares shown. How many Tombe and IWE Ltd shares does the trader purchase at current prices?
Which regional store sold the second highest number of new mobile phone contracts for the Platinum and Gold packages combined (over the previous 12 months)?
questions.explanation: Platinum + Gold totals are Central 9,394; Northern 9,730; Southern 9,707; Eastern 10,140; Western 9,441. Northern is second highest.

questions.prompt: If the price of each package was a one-off payment and not a monthly charge, what would the difference in revenue be between the package with the lowest number of sales and the package with the highest number of sales over the 12 month period, across all regions combined?
questions.explanation: Platinum has the lowest sales: 23,415 × £40 = £936,600. Silver has the highest sales: 26,162 × £30 = £784,860. The absolute difference is £936,600 - £784,860 = £151,740.

questions.prompt: What is the difference in average monthly sale values between the most and the least expensive packages? Referring to the initial cost of the package only and not subsequent monthly payments.
questions.explanation: Platinum annual value = 23,415 × £40 = £936,600, or £78,050 per month. Bronze annual value = 26,160 × £25 = £654,000, or £54,500 per month. Difference = £23,550.

questions.prompt: Assuming the only costs are those of the monthly package, what was the annual cost saving for a customer who switched from the Gold to the Bronze package?
questions.explanation: Monthly saving = £35 - £25 = £10. Annual saving = £10 × 12 = £120.

questions.prompt: Over the next twelve months the number of Bronze package sales increases by 12.5% and 25% for the Eastern and Southern regional stores respectively, whilst other sales remain the same. What are the total Bronze package sales for the next twelve months across all IK-Connections stores?
What is the average quarterly turnover for Syballe Sons compared to the Competitor Consultancy Firm across Quarters 1-4?
Between which two quarters was there the same percentage change in turnover for both Syballe Sons and the Competitor Consultancy Firm?
questions.explanation: From Quarter 4 to Next Quarter, Syballe rises from 10 to 12 and the competitor from 20 to 24. Both increases are 2/10 = 4/20 = 20%.

questions.prompt: The quarter immediately following the period shown will see Syballe Sons’ cost and turnover both increase by the same absolute amounts as between Quarter 4 and Next Quarter. What will be the difference between their turnover and costs in that following quarter?
questions.explanation: From Quarter 4 to Next Quarter turnover rises by 2 units and costs by 3. Applying those again gives turnover 14 and costs 14 (each in £10,000s), so there is no difference.

questions.prompt: In the Next Quarter a new competitor enters the market and takes 1/10th of Syballe Sons’ turnover, as well as 1/8th of the Competitor Consultancy’s turnover. What is the turnover for this new competitor in the Next Quarter?
If Gross Profit is Turnover minus Costs, what was the absolute difference in the Gross Profit between Syballe Sons and the Competitor Consultancy Firm for Quarters 1-4 inclusive?
What was Brand 2’s gross revenue in 2008?
questions.explanation: Brand 2 is 10% of 2008 total gross revenue of £44.4m: 0.10 × £44.4m = £4.44m = £4,440,000.

questions.prompt: Which Brand’s gross revenue has increased in value by the largest amount between 2006 and 2008?
questions.explanation: Brand 4 rises from 25% × £40m = £10m in 2006 to 35% × £44.4m = £15.54m in 2008, an increase of £5.54m. This exceeds Brand 1’s £3.32m increase; Brands 2 and 3 decrease.

questions.prompt: If Earnings per share = Pre-tax profit / Number of shares issued, how many shares were issued in 2008 compared to 2006?
questions.explanation: 2006 shares = £8.5m/£0.85 = 10m. 2008 shares = £9m/£1.20 = 7.5m. Therefore 2008 had 2.5m fewer shares.

questions.prompt: For the average annual pre-tax profit (for the years 2007-2009) to equal the average annual pre-tax profit (for the years 2007-2010), what must be the new 2010 Projection?
questions.explanation: The 2007-2009 average is (£8.7m + £9m + £9.6m)/3 = £9.1m. Adding a fourth value leaves the average unchanged only if that value is also £9.1m.

questions.prompt: In which year was pre-tax profit less than 20% of total gross revenue?
What are the total earnings for the working population in Spain?
questions.explanation: Spain’s population is 24.2m + 23.8m = 48m. The working population is 45% × 48m = 21.6m. Total earnings = 21.6m × €25,000 = €540bn.

questions.prompt: If the annual birth rates for Germany and Spain are 5.4 births (per 500 population) and 6.4 births (per 500 population) respectively, what is the difference between the number of Spanish and German babies born each year?
questions.explanation: Germany: 80m × 5.4/500 = 864,000 births. Spain: 48m × 6.4/500 = 614,400 births. Germany has 864,000 - 614,400 = 249,600 more babies.

questions.prompt: Which of the following countries has a non-working population that is closest in number to the UK’s non-working population?
questions.explanation: UK non-workers = 56m × 48% = 26.88m. Spain non-workers = 48m × 55% = 26.4m, only 0.48m away; the other differences are larger.

questions.prompt: If the ratio of French unemployed in urban to rural areas is 7:8 and the French unemployment rate is 12% of the working population, how many French unemployed are there in urban areas?
questions.explanation: France’s working population = (31.1m + 31.4m) × 48% = 30m. Unemployed = 12% × 30m = 3.6m. Urban unemployed = 7/15 × 3.6m = 1.68m.

questions.prompt: If the ratio of France:Belgium average earnings per head of working population is 2:5, then what is Belgium’s average earnings in £, at an exchange rate of 1.15 Euros to the £ (to the nearest £100)?

tests.description: A 30-question mixed-difficulty numerical reasoning test using employee, laptop, online-search, advertising, trade, and birth-rate data.
tests.instructions:

You will have to work quickly and accurately to perform well in this test. If you don't know the answer to a question, leave it and come back to it if you have time. Each question will have five possible answers, one of which is correct. You may click Back and Next during the test to review or skip questions.

You can submit your test at any time. If the time limit is up before you click submit the test will automatically be submitted with the answers you have selected. It is recommended to keep working until the time limit is up.

questions.prompt: Between which three years was there an average of 1,553 employees for one of the Subsidiary Companies?

In 2008 subsidiary company 4 comprised 2 regions with double the number of employees in one region compared to the other. If the ratio of male:female employees in the smaller region was 1:1.15, what was this region’s number of male employees?
questions.explanation: The smaller region has 1/3 of 1,548 = 516 employees. Male:female parts total 2.15, so males = 516/2.15 = 240.

questions.prompt: 1 in 15 of the parent company’s part-time employees were managers in 2005, and 1 in 13 part-time employees were managers in 2007. What was the difference in the number of part-time managers in 2005 compared to 2007?
questions.explanation: Total employees were 6,500 in both years. In 2005, 12% were part-time: 780, of whom 780/15 = 52 were managers. In 2007, 8% were part-time: 520, of whom 520/13 = 40 were managers. 2005 had 12 more.

questions.prompt: What % of the Parent Company’s total employees worked for Subsidiary 5 in 2006 (to the nearest whole %)?
In 2009 what was the absolute difference between the Parent Company’s full-time employees and part-time employees (if Number of employees = Full-time employees + part-time employees)?
questions.explanation: The 2009 total is 6,600. Part-time = 5% × 6,600 = 330 and full-time = 6,270. Difference = 6,270 - 330 = 5,940.

questions.prompt: For which laptop, or laptops, is the difference between the manufacturing cost and the design cost less than 20% of the manufacturing cost?
questions.explanation: The closest is Stunn: (£145 - £115)/£145 = 20.69%, which is still not less than 20%. Every other model has a larger percentage difference, so none qualify.

questions.prompt: Put the laptop models in order of increasing mark-up (Mark-up = Price – Costs).
questions.explanation: Mark-ups are Adele £350-(£140+£90)=£120; Stunn £160; Adelphi £175; Faze £200; Brete £325. Increasing order is Adele, Stunn, Adelphi, Faze, Brete.

questions.prompt: If the same number of each model was sold last month and total sales were £220,000, how many of each model were sold?
Which of the following would generate the highest total amount at the sale prices shown?
options: 150 Adele laptops at a further 60% reduction to the sale price
50 Faze and 50 Stunn laptops on sale
questions.explanation: Sale prices are Adele £262.50, Faze £152, Stunn £210 and Brete £433.33. Totals are A £19,687.50; B £15,750; C £18,100; D £19,500; E £18,900. A is highest.

questions.prompt: The current exchange rate for US Dollars to the Pound is 1.62 USD to 1 Pound. How much would it cost a customer in the USA to purchase a Faze laptop once a discount of 12% has been applied? Assuming that the USA prices are equivalent to that in the UK and do not include a sale price fraction.
questions.explanation: Discounted UK price = £380 × 0.88 = £334.40. Converted at $1.62 per £: £334.40 × 1.62 = $541.728, which rounds to $541.73.

questions.prompt: In which country was there the second highest number of people searching who were buying goods/services online?
questions.explanation: Buyer counts (thousands) are Australia 19,613×32%=6,276.16; Ireland 320.88; UK 6,869.5; Italy 1,188; Sweden 6,805.68. Sweden is second highest.

questions.prompt: In which country was there the second lowest number of people searching who were selling goods/services online?
questions.explanation: Seller counts (thousands) are Australia 1,961.3; Ireland 34.38; UK 3,747; Italy 891; Sweden 3,402.84. Italy is second lowest.

questions.prompt: Of those in the UK that buy goods/services online they spend on average £1.50 per month. Approximately, what is the total annual spend from this group of people?
questions.explanation: UK online buyers = 31.225m × 22% = 6.8695m. Annual spend = 6.8695m × £1.50 × 12 = £123.651m, approximately £124m.

questions.prompt: If the three countries I.U.I. (Ireland, UK, Italy) are grouped together and the other two countries S.A. (Sweden, Australia) are also grouped together, what is the difference between the total number of searches per I.U.I. country and the total number of searches per S.A. country?
questions.explanation: I.U.I. searches per country = (170 + 3,975 + 1,855)/3 = 2,000m. S.A. searches per country = (9,578 + 2,412)/2 = 5,995m. Difference = 3,995m.

questions.prompt: Which country has the lowest number of online searches per person searching?
questions.explanation: Searches per searcher are proportional to total searches (millions) divided by people (thousands): Australia ≈123.0, Ireland 148.3, UK 127.3, Italy 124.9, Sweden 591.1. Australia is lowest.

questions.prompt: Which of the following two media are predicted together to generate £6.15 billion of advertising revenue in 2011?
questions.explanation: Magazines and television total 9% + 21% = 30% of £20.5bn. £20.5bn × 30% = £6.15bn.

questions.prompt: If the Internet advertising forecast for 2011 is expected to split into mobile: display advertising in a 1:4 ratio, what is the mobile forecast?
questions.explanation: Internet forecast = 31% × £20.5bn = £6.355bn. Mobile is 1/(1+4) = 1/5, so £6.355bn/5 = £1.271bn ≈ £1.27bn.

questions.prompt: If the same absolute trends in advertising revenue from 2009 to 2010 continue for 2010 to 2011, then what will be the 2011 advertising revenue for Television and Internet combined?
questions.explanation: Television rises by £0.6bn, so 2011 is £4.9bn. Internet rises by £0.8bn, so 2011 is £7.1bn. Combined = £12.0bn.

questions.prompt: In which year, or years, was Television advertising revenue less than 22.5% of the year’s total advertising revenue?
If in 2009 an external market force had reduced the year’s advertising revenue from Newspapers by 10% and from the Internet by 20%, then what was the total 2009 advertising revenue?
questions.explanation: Adjusted 2009 values are Internet £5.5bn×80%=£4.4bn and Newspaper £6.1bn×90%=£5.49bn. Adding Television £3.7bn and Radio £1.2bn gives £14.79bn.

questions.prompt: Of the regions shown what was the difference between the highest and the lowest trade balance in 2008?
questions.explanation: 2008 balances are China $7,200m, UK $2,100m, Japan $4,900m, South America $1,600m and Russia $1,800m. Highest minus lowest = $7,200m - $1,600m = $5,600m.

questions.prompt: If Japan’s exports value increased by 1/5th between 2008 and 2009 then what was Japan’s imports value in 2009?
questions.explanation: Japan’s 2009 exports = $29,400m × 1.2 = $35,280m. Since trade balance = exports - imports and the 2009 balance is $5,840m, imports = $35,280m - $5,840m = $29,440m.

questions.prompt: Compared to 2009, the UK’s trade balance is expected to increase by 3.5% in 2010 and China’s trading balance is expected to decrease by 4.4%. What is the difference between the 2010 trade balance forecasts for these countries (to the nearest $million)?
questions.explanation: UK forecast = $1,825m × 1.035 = $1,888.875m. China forecast = $18,400m × 0.956 = $17,590.4m. Difference = $15,701.525m, which rounds to $15,702m.

questions.prompt: Which region or regions have experienced a decrease in their trade balance between 2008 and 2009?
questions.explanation: The UK falls from $2,100m to $1,825m and Russia from $1,800m to $1,200m. China, Japan and South America increase.

questions.prompt: What is the trading balance range (highest minus lowest) for the five regions between 2008-2009?
questions.explanation: Across both years, the highest balance is China 2009 at $18,400m and the lowest is Russia 2009 at $1,200m. The range is $18,400m - $1,200m = $17,200m.

questions.prompt: If the number of annual births are distributed evenly across the year and they remain constant at the levels shown, then how many months will it take for Outer London‘s population to increase by 245,000? (Ignoring death rate)
questions.explanation: Outer London has 35,811 + 34,189 = 70,000 births per year. At 70,000/12 births per month, 245,000 ÷ (70,000/12) = 42 months.

questions.prompt: Which country or countries shown have a population of less than 2.9 million people?
questions.explanation: Population = annual births ÷ birth rate × 1,000. Northern Ireland: 26,449/14.8×1,000 ≈ 1.787m; Wales: 35,440/12.5×1,000 = 2.8352m; Scotland ≈ 4.572m. Northern Ireland and Wales are below 2.9m.

questions.prompt: What is the population of Inner and Outer London combined (to the nearest 100,000)?
questions.explanation: Inner London population = 48,196/16.4×1,000 ≈ 2.9388m. Outer London = 70,000/15.1×1,000 ≈ 4.6358m. Combined ≈ 7.5745m, rounding to 7.6m.

questions.prompt: How many babies are born on average as twin births in Wales over five years? (Assume that the annual birth rate and number of births remains the same across the five years).
questions.explanation: Wales has 18,640 + 16,800 = 35,440 births yearly. Twin sets = 1.25% × 35,440 = 443; twin babies = 443 × 2 = 886 yearly. Over five years: 886 × 5 = 4,430.

questions.prompt: What percent of births are male across the 5 Regions shown?
questions.explanation: Across the five regions, male births total 178,690 and female births total 169,060. Male percentage = 178,690/(178,690 + 169,060) × 100 = 51.3846%, which rounds to 51.4%.
